According to @HRANA_English, 1,701 civilians were killed in the Iran war from its start on February 28 to the April 7 ceasefire, including at least 254 children.

An additional 714 deaths remain under review.
en-hrana.org/day-39-of-u-s-a…

“…dozens of refineries, storage facilities, and oil and gas fields in at least nine countries, from Iran to the UAE and beyond, have been targeted in strikes. All told, 10 percent or more of the world’s oil supply has been turned off.” nytimes.com/2026/04/08/busin…

So the Iranians are going to be making more money after this war...


Jonathan Karl (@jonkarl)

This morning, I asked President Trump if he’s okay with the Iranians charging a toll for all ships that go through the Strait of Hormuz, he told me there may be a Joint US-Iran venture to charge tolls:

“We’re thinking of doing it as a joint venture. It’s a way of securing it — also securing it from lots of other people.”

“It’s a beautiful thing”
